page: Amazon Web Services c8a.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated single-core, single-threaded AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running on x86_64 architecture at a clock speed of up to 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16 extensions), VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 2.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 RAM rated at 6 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio characteristic of compute-oriented profiles. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark measurements reflect the single-core topology of the instance. While aggregate multi-core throughput and overall PassMark metrics rank in the lower quartile due to the single-thread limit, single-core execution delivers strong results. In stress-ng single-core tests, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression, the server ranks within the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Memory read and write bandwidth for large blocks remain in the middle tier, achieving 47.05 GB/sec and 33.96 GB/sec respectively.

Given its minimal memory footprint and dedicated single-core compute performance, c8a.medium is suited for lightweight compute tasks, small-scale batch automation, single-threaded data compression, microservices, and modest static web serving where high clock frequency is prioritized over parallel capacity.

Configured with 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, the instance maintains a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio without attached local storage or GPU hardware. The CPU architecture supports vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 and SHA-NI. In performance benchmarks, single-core processing and compression tasks rank in the upper decile, whereas multi-core throughput and database transactions remain constrained by the single-thread configuration. Networking delivers a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, single-threaded processing pipelines, utilities, and static web serving.
